specification.objective: Align the TouchIn time-clock workspace with the supplied reference using the existing shared workspace design primitives, while preserving all punch, location, loading, and timeline behavior.

requirements.statement: The time-clock page must use the existing shared workspace header, section, status, and metric components with the TouchIn accent and typography.

At wide content widths, the time/status actions and location state must form a balanced split hero and the four existing metrics must appear in one row; at medium and narrow widths, both layouts must adapt without horizontal overflow.
The daily history must identify the current day and present a clear empty state without inventing records or changing pagination.
Existing punch actions, permission handling, work-log collection, errors, and accessibility feedback remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The page shows a concise CONTROLE DE PONTO overline, a horizontally split hero at desktop width, and four shared metric cards in a single desktop row.
At narrow widths the hero stacks and the metric grid reduces to two columns or one column as available width requires, with no render overflow.
The daily timeline displays a current-date indicator and a visually distinct empty state while retaining the existing empty-state copy and real event rendering.
All existing time-clock, location, accessibility, work-log, loading, pagination, lint, release-build, and browser smoke validations pass.

invariants.statement: No punch state transitions, location permission requirements, geolocation data, or API behavior change.
Existing shared workspace components and app theme remain the source of visual styling; no new dependency or unrelated page redesign is added.
The time-clock page retains its existing loading, retry, error, timeline pagination, and work-log flows.

forbidden_states.statement: Wide desktop leaves the four existing time metrics unnecessarily split into two rows.
The hero or metric row overflows on supported narrow screens.
The redesign invents time-clock data, alters punch behavior, or weakens location/accessibility safeguards.

inputs.statement: Viewport width, existing time-clock controller state, and location permission state.
The supplied time-clock design reference and existing shared workspace components.

outputs.statement: A responsive time-clock workspace visually aligned with the design reference and existing TouchIn workspace style.
Widget regression coverage for wide and narrow layout behavior.

failure_semantics.statement: A failed time-clock data load keeps its existing visible retry path.
If responsive constraints cannot fit the wide composition, the page falls back to a stacked layout instead of clipping or overflowing.

argv: time-clock reference layout adapts across viewport sizes
